statBlock.name: Asharra
statBlock.description: The elderly aarakocra whom Kir Sabal calls Teacher. She shelters the surviving heirs to Omu and can grant travelers flight for the journey to the city.

sections.Traits: Dive Attack. While flying, dive at least 30 ft. straight toward a target. A melee weapon hit against that target then deals 3 (1d6) extra damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Asharra is a 5th-level druid spellcaster using Wisdom (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Druidcraft, Mending, Produce Flame.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Faerie Fire, Thunderwave.
2nd level (3 slots). Gust of Wind, Hold Person, Lesser Restoration.
3rd level (2 slots). Call Lightning, Wind Wall.
sections.Actions:
Talon. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) slashing damage.
Javelin. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Summon Air Elemental. Five aarakocra must stay within 30 ft. of one another and each spend their action and movement on an aerial dance for three consecutive turns. Each must maintain Concentration as if on a spell. Once all five complete the dance, an Air Elemental appears in an empty space within 60 ft. of the group, is friendly toward them, and follows spoken orders. It stays for 1 hour, until it dies, all its summoners die, or any summoner dismisses it as a bonus action. Each participant must finish a short rest before performing the dance again. When the elemental returns to the Elemental Plane of Air, any aarakocra within 5 ft. of it may go along.
sections.Dance of the Seven Winds: This 10-minute ritual requires an aarakocra elder, seven other aarakocra to chant without interruption, and a black orchid. Asharra grinds and inhales the orchid, then dances around up to ten creatures that cannot fly. Her wings disappear when the rite ends and each recipient gains a magical fly speed of 30 ft., enough to travel 4 miles per hour. After three days the recipients lose the flight and Asharra regains her wings and flying speed.
sections.Encounter context: Asharra offers the rite to travelers heading to Omu to destroy the Soulmonger. She directs them to find the orchid in Nangalore, whose Eblis have kept her people away. Kir Sabal also shelters Mwaxanaré and Na.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 69. Asharra uses the 2014 Aarakocra stat block with the changes printed in the Kir Sabal encounter.

statBlock.name: Assassin Vine
statBlock.description: A creeping plant that constricts its prey and feeds the soil around its roots. Bitter grapes can hang from its smaller vines, and underground specimens hide among fungi in warm caverns.

sections.Traits: False Appearance. A motionless assassin vine looks like an ordinary plant.
sections.Actions:
Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 20 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage and grapple the target (escape DC 14). Until the grapple ends, the target is restrained and takes 21 (6d6) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The vine can constrict one target at a time.
Entangling Vines. Animate roots and vines in a 15-ft. square on the ground within 30 ft. The square becomes difficult terrain. Creatures in the square when the effect begins must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or become restrained. A creature restrained this way can take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check to escape. The terrain and restraints last for 1 minute, until the vine dies, or until it uses the action again.

statBlock.name: Atropal
statBlock.description: An abandoned, unfinished godling that drifts above the ground. Its withered cord draws on the Negative Plane. The specimen in the Tomb of the Nine Gods feeds on souls captured by the Soulmonger.

sections.Languages: Understands Celestial. Its utterances are incoherent.
sections.Damage immunities: Cold, necrotic. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Negative Energy Aura. Creatures within 30 ft. cannot regain hit points. A creature starting its turn within that distance takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. On a hit with a Vorpal Sword or another vorpal weapon, the attacker may sever the atropal’s cord in place of dealing damage. The atropal then loses this aura.
Turn Resistance Aura. The atropal and other undead within 30 ft. have advantage on saves against turning effects.
Undead Nature. The atropal needs no air, food, drink, or sleep. It cannot be raised or resurrected.
sections.Actions:
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.
Ray of Cold. Ranged spell attack, +12 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (6d6) cold damage.
Life Drain. Choose one visible creature within 120 ft. It makes a DC 19 Constitution save, taking 36 (8d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. The atropal regains half the hit points it dealt in damage.
Summon Wraith (Recharge 6). A Wraith appears in an empty space the atropal can see within 30 ft. It obeys the atropal, and only the atropal can control it. It disappears at 0 HP or when the atropal dies.
sections.Legendary actions:
The atropal has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn.
Touch (1 action). Make a Touch attack.
Ray of Cold (2 actions). Use Ray of Cold.
Wail (3 actions). Each creature within 120 ft. that can hear the wail must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution save or gain one level of exhaustion.
sections.Death God’s Nursery: The atropal attacks creatures that threaten it or the Soulmonger. Killing the atropal brings Acererak to the south balcony. Destroying the Soulmonger ends the death curse and releases its trapped souls. A creature entering the lava by falling into it or starting its turn there takes 55 (10d10) fire damage.
sections.Soulmonger: The crystal cylinder is a Huge object (AC 15, 200 HP) vulnerable to radiant damage and immune to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Any one of its three adamantine struts breaking brings the whole device down. Each strut is a Large object (AC 20, 100 HP) immune to fire, poison, psychic, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. A creature taking damage while standing on a strut must make a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall into the lava unless secured. When a strut breaks, unsecured creatures on it fall. One within reach of a balcony can leap to safety on a successful DC 10 Dexterity save.
sections.Soulmonger tentacles: Once per turn, the Soulmonger responds to a melee weapon hit on the cylinder or a strut with one tentacle attack against the attacker. Reach 30 ft., +7 to hit, 24 (4d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. It can grapple in place of damage (escape DC 16). If the grappled creature weighs up to 330 lb., the tentacle can also move it to an empty space within reach or drop it into the lava. Each tentacle is a Huge animated object (Strength 22, AC 15, 30 HP) immune to poison and psychic damage.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 214–215, with the Soulmonger encounter on pp. 184–186. Condition immunities follow the printed p. 214 block.

statBlock.name: Bag of Nails
statBlock.description: An elderly tabaxi hunter who picks off travelers from the roofs of Omu. He came to find the Navel of the Moon in hopes of locating his missing son.

sections.Traits:
Feline Agility. When Bag of Nails moves on his turn in combat, he can double his speed until that turn ends. He regains use after a turn when he moves 0 ft.
Assassinate. On his first turn he has advantage against creatures that have yet to act. His hits against surprised creatures are critical hits.
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, he takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Sneak Attack (1/turn). Add 14 (4d6) damage to a successful weapon attack if he has advantage. He can also add it if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of the target and he lacks disadvantage on the attack.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 2 (1d4) slashing damage.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. Apply the same poison save and damage as the Shortsword attack.
sections.Fallen Tree ambush: Bag of Nails begins hidden on the east bank, 150 ft. from the fallen tree bridge (DC 22 Wisdom (Perception) to spot him). He shoots when someone crosses and tries to hide at a new firing position after each shot. Below 39 HP, he surrenders and invites his enemies into his lair for stew. A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) check exposes his intent. The stew contains Midnight Tears. If it has not been neutralized by midnight, the eater makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 31 (9d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Five more doses can be found in the lair.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 102. The Fallen Tree encounter prints changes to the 2014 Assassin, including the claw attack and longbow.

statBlock.name: Chwinga
statBlock.description: A shy nature spirit about six inches tall. It peers out from rocks, plants, and streams, sometimes following a traveler to see what they do with their tools.

sections.Traits:
Evasion. When a Dexterity save would halve damage, the chwinga takes none on a success and half on a failure.
Unusual Nature. Chwingas sleep and need no air, food, or drink. When one dies, choose what remains: flower petals, a puff of pollen, a tiny statuette, a smooth stone, or fresh water.
sections.Spellcasting: Innate Spellcasting. Wisdom is the chwinga’s spellcasting ability. It needs no verbal or material components. At will: Druidcraft, Guidance, Pass without Trace, Resistance.
sections.Actions:
Magical Gift (1/day). Choose a humanoid the chwinga can see within 5 ft. The DM chooses one supernatural charm for that humanoid.
Natural Shelter. Enter a rock, living plant, or natural source of fresh water in the chwinga’s space. Attacks, spells, and other effects cannot target it while it is sheltered, and its blindsight still works. It can emerge as an action. Destroying the shelter puts the unharmed chwinga in the shelter’s space.
sections.Charm of Restoration: The chwinga in Nangalore’s eastern spirit dome can favor the tallest party member with this gift. It has 6 charges. As an action, spend 4 charges to cast Greater Restoration or 2 to cast Lesser Restoration. The charm disappears when its charges are spent.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 216–217. See p. 77 for Nangalore’s charm and p. 104 for the wagon encounter. Supernatural charms are in the Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), chapter 7.
sections.Encounter context: In Omu, a chwinga shelters in a mossy disk beneath an overturned wagon. It comes out if travelers leave an offering or follows them secretly if they pass by. It favors curly hair or beards. Vegepygmies flee once they notice it with the party. It stays outside shrines and dungeons.

statBlock.name: Clay Gladiator
statBlock.description: A painted clay guardian of Shagambi’s shrine. It bears a bronze spear and a wooden shield, and returns to its cell when destroyed.

sections.Traits:
Climbing. It can climb difficult surfaces and ceilings without a check.
Steadfast. It cannot be disarmed or make ranged attacks.
Brute. Its melee weapon hits include an extra weapon damage die, already counted below.
Construct Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep and cannot speak.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Spear. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage, or 13 (2d8 + 4) when wielded with two hands.
Shield Bash. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 9 (2d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Reactions: Parry. Add 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. It must see the attacker and hold a melee weapon.
sections.Shagambi’s shrine: Four cells hold one guardian apiece. At least 50 lb. on the pit’s pressure plate raises the cell gates and calls the guardians. A gladiator fights if attacked or called to the pit. It cannot leave the shrine. At 0 HP outside the pit, it and its gear disappear and it immediately reforms in its cell at full health with spear and shield. It can then return to the pit. A gladiator destroyed in the pit leaves its spear behind as it reforms. If a spear leaves the shrine, it returns to the gladiator’s hand. When no other creatures remain inside, the gladiators return to their cells and the gates close. Place one spear from each guardian in the four warrior statues to free Shagambi’s puzzle cube.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 100. The shrine gives changes to the 2014 Gladiator stat block and separate reformation rules.
